subtopicTitle: Systems of linear equations — matrix form Ax = b

cards.front: What is a system of linear equations?
cards.back: A collection of one or more linear equations involving the same set of variables. A linear equation is an algebraic equation in which each term is either a constant or the product of a constant and a single variable (to the first power).

cards.front:
Convert the system below into the matrix form $Ax=b$:
$2x_1 - 3x_2 + x_3 = 7$
$x_1 + 4x_2 - 2x_3 = -1$
cards.back:
The matrix form is:
$$A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 \end{pmatrix}, \quad x = \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad b = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$
So, the complete matrix equation is:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

cards.front: In the matrix equation $Ax=b$, what do $A$, $x$, and $b$ represent?
cards.back:
• $A$ is the coefficient matrix, containing the coefficients of the variables.
  • $x$ is the variable vector (or solution vector), containing the variables of the system.
  • $b$ is the constant vector (or right-hand side vector), containing the constants from the right-hand side of the equations.

cards.front: A vector $x_0$ is a solution to $Ax=b$ if...
cards.back: ...when $x_0$ is substituted into the matrix equation, the equality holds true. That is, $A x_0 = b$. This means that $x_0$ is a vector of values for the variables that simultaneously satisfies all equations in the system.

cards.front: Geometrically, what does each row of $Ax=b$ represent in 2D or 3D space?
cards.back: Each row of the matrix equation $Ax=b$ corresponds to a single linear equation. In 2D, each equation represents a line. In 3D, each equation represents a plane. A solution $x$ (if one exists) is the point (or line/plane) of intersection of all these lines/planes.

cards.front: Explain the matrix equation $Ax=b$ from the perspective of linear combinations of column vectors of $A$.
cards.back:
If $A = \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & a_2 & \dots & a_n \end{pmatrix}$ where $a_i$ are the column vectors of $A$, and $x = \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end{pmatrix}$, then $Ax=b$ can be written as:
$$x_1 a_1 + x_2 a_2 + \dots + x_n a_n = b$$
This means that $b$ must be a linear combination of the column vectors of $A$. A solution $x$ exists if and only if $b$ lies within the span of the column vectors of $A$.

cards.front: What is an augmented matrix $[A|b]$ and what is its primary purpose in solving $Ax=b$?
cards.back:
An augmented matrix $[A|b]$ is formed by appending the constant vector $b$ to the coefficient matrix $A$ as an additional column. For example, if $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and $b = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$, then $[A|b] = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & | & 6 \end{pmatrix}$.
Its primary purpose is to provide a compact notation for performing row operations (like Gaussian elimination) on the entire system of equations simultaneously, making it easier to find the solution(s) for $x$.
